references.text: God himself describes the Israelites' action with the golden calf and uses almost identical wording: 'This is your god, O Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'
Moses recounts the incident with the golden calf and confirms that the people cast a calf made of metal.
King Jeroboam made two golden calves and used the same expression: 'Here is your god, O Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'
Nehemiah refers to how the Israelites made for themselves a molten calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt.'
The psalm describes how the Israelites made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast image, exchanging their glory for the likeness of an ox.
Isaiah describes the process of casting an idol, which parallels how the golden calf was made.
Hosea refers directly to the calf in Samaria and condemns the idolatry that began with the golden calf.
Stephen quotes the incident in his speech: they made a calf in those days, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in what their hands had made.
Paul describes how people exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal creatures, reflecting the sin of the golden calf.
The verses belong to the same event; while verse 4 shows the people's idolatry, verse 24 shows Moses' attempt to explain away the sin.
Theological contrast: Leviticus confirms God's ownership based on the deliverance from Egypt, while Exodus 32 shows the breaking of this bond.
Direct continuation of the same event; it shows the consequence and God's judgment against the idol created in verse 4.
